title: VPC deploy field journal
content:
Quick personal journal / scratchpad for on-site VPC + on-prem deploys (notes to self).

Context: customer environment with split-horizon DNS and an MPLS connection to cloud region. This is a lightweight log — messy, meant for handoff.

---

TOPLINES / things to check first:
- Confirm customer allowed IP ranges for control-plane (we need both 52.23.x.x and our VPN exit IPs)
- Does their perimeter FW support source/destination NAT for the host network? If no, need CIDR mapping doc.
- K8s versions: customer cluster currently 1.22 (one node old), we require >=1.23 for driver-kit. Note: can run with workaround but watch kube-proxy mode.
- GPU nodes: customer uses mixed NVIDIA drivers (470 + 515) — will cause CUDA mismatch for our runtime images. Schedule driver upgrade or isolate on nodepool.
- Time sync: ntp/chrony must be consistent or image pulls fail with cert validation.

DAY LOGS
2024-01-26 09:20 - Arrival / kickoff call- Site contact: Rajesh P. / infra- Rack info: 2 x DGX-ish hosts (racked), 10G to aggregation, jumbo frames not enabled by default- Immediate ask: need to enable MTU 9000 between host <-> switch for large model shards.

Notes to self: check switch model, ask for spare port to test MTU. If can't enable, set batch size lower and enable token-limited fallback.

2024-01-26 11:05 - First deploy attempt (lab namespace)- Applied helm chart v0.9.2 (local patch applied for tolerations)- Problems: pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff for model-server: nvidia-container-runtime not found.
Troubleshooting steps taken:
  - ssh into node -> docker info shows runtime runc only. Customer uses containerd with nvidia/containerd integration not installed.
  - attempted 'ctr run' test -> fails.
Action: need SRE push to node to install nvidia-container-toolkit (containerd config) or we provide an init script. Raised JIRA-PD-89.

2024-01-27 08:40 - Network issues surfaced- Some control-plane requests to our hosted console failing with 502 on the customer's proxy.
Hypothesis: proxy is doing HTTPS inspection and resigning certs -> our client rejects.
Quick fix: switch to our fallback region endpoint over peered MPLS (private path). Need to confirm routing table entries.

Commands I ran / want to remember:
- Verify node driver: ssh root@node01 'nvidia-smi || echo no-driver'
- Check mtu: ip link show dev eth0 | grep mtu
- kubelet logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager- docker/containerd config: cat /etc/containerd/config.toml | grep nvidia -n

Open blockers (customer action required):
- FW: allow egress to S3 signing endpoints (s3.amazonaws.com) for model pull, OR we set up local model registry. Customer: "no internet egress by default". Need signed approval.
- Install nvidia-container-toolkit on containerd hosts (customer infra team)
- Permit subnet for control-plane callbacks: add 3 IPs to allowlist (listed in Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234).

Short TODOs (for me):
- [ ] Draft one-page runbook for node prep (drivers, containerd config, sysctl, docker tweaks) — use snippets from repo PR#512
- [ ] Create local model-registry tarball and verify pull from internal registry (workaround if S3 blocked)
- [ ] Test MTU fallback: simulate 1.5k MTU and ensure infer latency within SLO with smaller batch
- [ ] Coordinate with Solutions Eng for canary rollout (2 nodes) after driver fix

Notes — commands/snippets to put in runbook:
1) containerd + nvidia helper (example):
   curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-container-runtime/gpgkey | sudo apt-key add -
   distribution=$(lsb_release -cs)
   curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list
   sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
   sudo systemctl restart containerd

2) sysctl settings we recommend (append to /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood.conf):
   net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
   net.core.somaxconn=1024
   fs.file-max=100000

3) kubelet args (note for customer's kops/terraform):
   --allowed-unsafe-sysctls=net.core.somaxconn

Quick tip: if using Calico, check felix MTU and IPIP mode — IPIP introduces -20 bytes overhead; tune MTU accordingly.

Customer env reminders (sensitive config bits to confirm):
- DNS: internal domain suffix svc.finbank.local -> must resolve our internal model-registry host or we fall back to IPs- LDAP single-sign on for console access -> need test account- HSM: they will not give private key but offered signed certs for TLS termination. Confirm cert chain includes intermediate CA.

Weird intermittent: occasional model export failing with HTTP 403 from S3 when payload > 100MB. Hypothesis: proxy content-length rewrite or token expiry. Repro steps saved in linked artifact PR/issue.

Hand-off notes for next on-call (Samira):
- Key path: /opt/redwood/deploy-scripts/field-prep.sh (small bootstrap) — run as root, will install drivers and set containerd config
- Contact Rajesh for switch MTU enable (port 14). If they refuse, we must disable jumbo frames in our shard handshake and add batch-size limiter env var: RW_BATCH_MAX=64
- If gateway proxy signs certs, set REDWOOD_API_TRUSTED_CA to their CA bundle and rotate keys later

Unresolved questions to add to Confluence:
- Can we get a per-tenant local model cache that doesn't require S3? (perf and compliance ask)
- Should we add an automatic driver healthcheck to runtime agent (preflight)? Pro: reduces field time. Con: increases agent complexity.

End-of-day quick retrospective:
- Wins: got rack network checked, validated node hardware and PCIe lane counts, captured driver mismatch case- Misses: underestimated customer's proxy restrictions -> had to implement multiple fallbacks

Next steps for me:
- Finish runbook draft and push to CONFLUENCE-1234 by 2024-01-28
- Add a tiny containerd post-install script to our repo and reference in PR#512
- Schedule call with customer infra to unblock FW + driver install

Random note to self: follow up on license for their offline content-signing (legal needs input).

---

Loose brain-dump ends here. Keep this very short when handing to Solutions Eng — strip troubleshooting logs.
